newsitem.title: USA: Sun Puerto Rico hurricane watch intensifies.
newsitem.headline: Sun Puerto Rico hurricane watch intensifies.

text.p: Sun Oil Co, faced with Hurricane Hortense's unexpectedly northerly position, said it is intensifying its watch on the storm amid forecasts it could come near Sun's refinery on the island.

Sun spokesman Bud Davis said the hurricane watch at Sun's 85,000 barrel per day refinery in Yabucoa on the island had eased earlier Monday as forecasts projected storm would pass south of Puerto Rico.
"They're watching the storm a bit more closely now," he said, noting refinery operators were trimming back some of the output at the plant's units, though not significantly.
"They're in a position of shutting it down rather quickly if necessary," Davis said.
Output from the Sun refinery is largely destined for markets on Puerto Rico.

At 1100 EDT/1500 GMT, the storm was about 135 miles 220 kilometres southeast of Ponce, Puerto Rico as it moved west at six miles per hour (mph)/nine kilometres per hour (kph) while packing sustained winds of 80 mph/130 kph.
"The forecast track brings hurricane-force winds dangerously close to portions of Puerto Rico," the National Hurricane Center said.
But Hortense remained a weak Category 1 hurricane, according to National Hurricane Center.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
